title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
author: Kehong Gong, Xiaoxu Zheng, Guanli Hou, Seunghun Lee et al.

summary: Robot agents built on vision-language models depend on both the planner and its harness: the tools, feedback, memory, and recovery logic around it. Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost?
takeaways: Can improvements to a large teacher's harness be carried into a compact agent with lower inference compute cost?

We first freeze an open-weight teacher and improve its harness through recursive self-improvement (RSI): frontier LLM agents read the teacher's trajectories and propose harness edits, and each edit is accepted only if it passes a paired statistical test.
On identical episodes, the final 4B student outperforms open 4B agents, the open 27B harness-RSI model SenseNova-RoboRSI, and our own teacher model placed in three competitors' harnesses.
